finding.cause: Final auth checks used PostgreSQL transaction-start now(), so a user-row wait could cross a session or challenge deadline without invalidating proof.
finding.fix: Use clock_timestamp() in four final session/challenge authorization queries after the user lock. API errors, revocation, MFA, locking order and proof lifetimes otherwise unchanged.
tests: absolute session expiry while waiting rejects email-verification request with401 SESSION_REQUIRED, without challenge/outbox/audit
idle session expiry while waiting rejects email-verification request with401 SESSION_REQUIRED, without challenge/outbox/audit
expired MFA challenge cannot mint a session or consume authenticator state
expired password-reset challenge cannot replace password or revoke sessions
expired email-verification challenge cannot verify address or consume proof
finding.database: real PostgreSQL16.15 plus pgvector0.6, isolated schema, no clock/SQL mocks

reviewedControls: Public signup uses strict schema and server-fixed customer role.
Administrator and target authorization, MFA and last active owner protections rechecked under locks.
Password and permission changes revoke existing sessions and challenges.
Env provisioning requires database owner and immutable identity bindings; normal reruns preserve panel edits.
Uploads enforce hard per-file limit, admin-defined per-type/user/site quota, bounded concurrency, reservations and commit-time auth/policy checks.
Stored uploads use random server-generated names, exclusive0600 writes, fsync and rollback/reconciliation.
Private media access rechecks current actor and ownership; non-image media requires clean scan.
Restore security requires owner connection, invalidates old sessions/challenges/recovery codes/invitations and reconciles access.
limitations: Static review is scoped; not a claim of a complete security audit.
The PostgreSQL gate used real disposable PostgreSQL and the API gate exercised in-process HTTP handlers; neither alone proves deployment readiness on a customer server.
The exact cause of the prior shared-process runner early exit remains unconfirmed; the accepted run used default process isolation and serial concurrency.
No paid AI, real SMTP, public deployment or new-host recovery was performed by this agent.
